Corn___Cercospora_leaf_spot.symptoms: Small, tan to brown rectangular lesions that run parallel to leaf veins, eventually coalescing to blight large portions of leaves.
Corn___Cercospora_leaf_spot.possible_causes: Fungus Cercospora zeae-maydis surviving in surface crop residue during warm, humid weather (25-30°C).
prevention: Select disease-resistant or tolerant corn hybrids.
Implement 2-year crop rotation with non-host crops like soybean.
Till surface crop residues into soil where feasible.
management: Apply recommended strobilurin or triazole fungicides at VT-R1 stage when lesions reach third leaf below ear.
Ensure adequate potassium levels to strengthen stalks and foliage.
Improve drainage and spacing to minimize canopy humidity.

Corn___Common_rust.symptoms: Oval to elongated reddish-brown pustules (uredinia) scattered on both upper and lower leaf surfaces, rupturing the epidermis.
Corn___Common_rust.possible_causes: Fungus Puccinia sorghi transported by wind currents during moderate temperatures (16-25°C) and high humidity.
prevention: Plant resistant maize hybrids with Rp-resistance genes.
Early planting to avoid high airborne spore loads late in season.
Monitor weather forecasts during vegetative growth.
management: Apply foliar fungicides (Azoxystrobin or Pyraclostrobin) if pustules appear prior to tasseling on susceptible hybrids.
Maintain balanced soil fertility (avoid excess nitrogen).

Corn___Northern_Leaf_Blight.symptoms: Long, elliptical cigar-shaped grayish-green to tan lesions (2.5 to 15 cm long) starting on lower leaves and moving upward.
Corn___Northern_Leaf_Blight.possible_causes: Fungus Exserohilum turcicum thriving in wet, cool-to-moderate conditions (18-27°C).
prevention: Use multi-genic resistant corn hybrids.
Rotate fields out of corn for at least 1-2 years.
Incorporate infected residues through deep tillage.
management: Spray Mancozeb 75 WP (2 g/L) or Propiconazole 25 EC (1 ml/L) upon early detection.
Consult local Krishi Vigyan Kendra (KVK) for regional spray thresholds.

Corn___Healthy.symptoms: Deep green, vigorous leaves with no necrotic lesions, pustules, or discoloration.
Corn___Healthy.possible_causes: Optimal nutrient management, clean seed, and favorable environmental conditions.
prevention: Continue balanced NPK fertilisation (120:60:40 kg/ha).
Maintain regular scouting schedule every 7-10 days.
management: No chemical intervention needed.
Irrigate at critical knee-high and silking stages.

Pepper___Bacterial_spot.symptoms: Small, water-soaked, dark green circular spots on leaves that turn dark brown with yellow halos; severe defoliation occurs.
Pepper___Bacterial_spot.possible_causes: Bacterium Xanthomonas campestris pv. vesicatoria spread by splashing rain, wind, and contaminated tools.
prevention: Use certified disease-free seeds and hot-water treated seedlings (50°C for 25 min).
Disinfect greenhouse trays, stakes, and tools before transplanting.
Avoid overhead sprinkler irrigation.
management: Spray copper hydroxide (2 g/L) mixed with Streptocycline (0.1 g/L) at first symptom onset.
Remove and safely destroy heavily infected plants.
Practice 2-3 year crop rotation away from solanaceous crops.

Pepper___Healthy.symptoms: Firm, upright green foliage without spots, leaf drop, or vein clearing.
Pepper___Healthy.possible_causes: Proper cultural care, clean seed stock, and good soil aeration.
prevention: Maintain mulching to suppress weeds and splash dispersal.
Ensure consistent soil moisture without waterlogging.
management: No chemical treatment required.
Apply organic bio-stimulants or neem oil preventively.

Potato___Early_blight.symptoms: Small, dark brown to black spots with characteristic concentric rings ('target board' pattern) appearing first on older lower leaves.
Potato___Early_blight.possible_causes: Fungus Alternaria solani surviving in crop debris and solanaceous weeds.
prevention: Plant certified pathogen-free seed tubers.
Ensure 3-year crop rotation with legumes or cereals.
Maintain optimal potassium and nitrogen nutrition to avoid plant stress.
management: Apply Mancozeb 75 WP @ 2.5 g/L or Chlorothalonil 75 WP @ 2 g/L at 7-10 day intervals.
Remove and burn senescing lower leaves with severe infection.
Kill vines 10-14 days before harvest to prevent tuber infection.

Potato___Late_blight.symptoms: Water-soaked, pale to dark green lesions turning purplish-black rapidly; white fungal downy growth visible on leaf undersides in humid conditions.
Potato___Late_blight.possible_causes: Oomycete Phytophthora infestans favored by cool temperatures (12-20°C) and relative humidity >90%.
prevention: Plant certified resistant varieties (e.g. Kufri Girdhari, Kufri Himalini).
Eliminate cull piles and volunteer potato plants.
Ensure hilling to provide thick soil coverage over developing tubers.
management: Spray systemic fungicide Metalaxyl 8% + Mancozeb 64% WP (Ridomil Gold) @ 2.5 g/L immediately.
Follow with contact fungicides (Cymoxanil + Mancozeb).
Never irrigate in the late afternoon or evening.

Potato___Healthy.symptoms: Vibrant green canopy, sturdy stems, and no necrotic lesions or tuber rot symptoms.
Potato___Healthy.possible_causes: Optimal seed treatment, proper ridging, and balanced fertilisation.
prevention: Maintain ridging height to protect tubers from sunlight and blight spores.
Monitor local agrometeorological alerts for late blight risk.
management: No chemical fungicide needed.
Maintain steady soil moisture during tuber bulking.

Rice___Bacterial_leaf_blight.symptoms: Water-soaked stripes starting from leaf tips and margins, expanding into wavy, yellowish-white lesions with bacterial ooze beads on young lesions.
Rice___Bacterial_leaf_blight.possible_causes: Bacterium Xanthomonas oryzae pv. oryzae transmitted through irrigation water and severe rainstorms.
prevention: Grow BLB-resistant cultivars (e.g. Improved Samba Mahsuri, PR-126).
Avoid high doses of nitrogenous fertilizers.
Drain field water intermittently to aerate root systems.
management: Spray Copper Oxychloride 50 WP (2.5 g/L) + Streptocycline (0.15 g/L) at first symptom onset.
Apply MOP (Muriate of Potash) @ 25 kg/ha to improve disease resistance.
Avoid clipping seedling leaf tips during transplanting.

Rice___Brown_spot.symptoms: Oval or circular dark brown lesions with gray to whitish centers, resembling sesame seeds on leaf blades and glumes.
Rice___Brown_spot.possible_causes: Fungus Bipolaris oryzae (Cochliobolus miyabeanus) associated with nutrient-deficient, poorly drained, or drought-stressed soils.
prevention: Treat seed with Carbendazim 50 WP (2 g/kg seed) before sowing.
Correct soil deficiencies, especially potassium, silica, and zinc.
Maintain uniform standing water to reduce plant moisture stress.
management: Foliar spray of Propiconazole 25 EC (1 ml/L) or Tricyclazole 75 WP (0.6 g/L).
Apply balanced NPK with micronutrient blend (Zinc sulphate @ 25 kg/ha).

Rice___Leaf_smut.symptoms: Small, angular black, raised spots scattered across leaf blades; ruptured spots release black powdery mass of teliospores.
Rice___Leaf_smut.possible_causes: Fungus Entyloma oryzae prevalent in high-nitrogen, densely planted crops late in the season.
prevention: Avoid excessive nitrogen application.
Adopt recommended row spacing (20 x 15 cm) for airflow.
Deep plow stubble after harvest.
management: Usually minor; apply Mancozeb 75 WP (2 g/L) if infection reaches upper flag leaves.
Ensure timely harvest once grains reach physiological maturity.

Rice___Healthy.symptoms: Uniform emerald-green canopy with clean tillers and no necrotic spots or bacterial ooze.
Rice___Healthy.possible_causes: Certified treated seed, balanced basal nutrition, and disciplined water management.
prevention: Adopt Alternate Wetting and Drying (AWD) water management.
Scout weekly for stem borer and blast symptoms.
management: No chemical intervention needed.
Apply scheduled top dressing of nitrogen (Urea) at tillering and panicle initiation.

Tomato___Bacterial_spot.symptoms: Small, greasy, circular spots (<3 mm) on leaves, stems, and fruit; leaves turn yellow and drop prematurely.
Tomato___Bacterial_spot.possible_causes: Bacterium Xanthomonas vesicatoria transmitted via seed and water splash in warm, wet weather.
prevention: Use certified disease-free seeds or hot-water seed treatment.
Disinfect nursery trays and stakes with 10% sodium hypochlorite.
Do not work in fields when foliage is wet.
management: Spray Copper Oxychloride 50 WP (2.5 g/L) + Streptocycline (0.1 g/L) at weekly intervals.
Prune and safely destroy lower infected suckers and leaves.
Implement 3-year crop rotation away from solanaceous plants.

Tomato___Early_blight.symptoms: Dark brown circular spots with distinct concentric rings ('target board') and yellow chlorotic halos, beginning on older lower leaves.
Tomato___Early_blight.possible_causes: Fungus Alternaria solani surviving in crop residue, favored by warm temperatures (24-29°C) and humid conditions.
prevention: Stake plants and mulch soil with clean straw or plastic.
Prune lower leaves up to 30 cm from ground level.
Practice 3-year crop rotation with non-solanaceous crops.
management: Spray Mancozeb 75 WP @ 2.5 g/L or Chlorothalonil 75 WP @ 2 g/L at 7-10 day intervals.
Apply bio-fungicide Trichoderma harzianum as root dip and soil drench.
Avoid overhead irrigation; use drip irrigation systems.

Tomato___Late_blight.symptoms: Large, irregular water-soaked greenish-black lesions on leaves and stems; white moldy growth appears on undersides during wet conditions; fruit develops greasy brown rot.
Tomato___Late_blight.possible_causes: Oomycete Phytophthora infestans triggered by cool, wet weather (15-22°C with high humidity).
prevention: Plant resistant tomato hybrids (e.g. Arka Rakshak, Arka Samrat).
Provide wide row spacing (90 x 60 cm) for canopy ventilation.
Avoid planting adjacent to potato fields.
management: Immediately spray Cymoxanil 8% + Mancozeb 64% WP @ 2.5 g/L.
Alternate with Dimethomorph 50 WP (1 g/L) in high-pressure periods.
Remove and destroy severely affected plants to halt spore dispersal.

Tomato___Leaf_Mold.symptoms: Pale greenish-yellow spots with indistinct margins on upper leaf surfaces; olive-green to brown velvety fungal growth on corresponding lower surfaces.
Tomato___Leaf_Mold.possible_causes: Fungus Passalora fulva (Cladosporium fulvum) common in greenhouse and high-density humid plantings (>85% RH).
prevention: Ensure vigorous greenhouse ventilation and air circulation.
Space plants adequately to reduce humidity within canopy.
Avoid wetting foliage during watering.
management: Spray Copper Hydroxide (2 g/L) or Difenoconazole 25 EC (0.5 ml/L).
Ventilate and heat greenhouses to lower relative humidity below 80%.

Tomato___Septoria_leaf_spot.symptoms: Numerous small circular spots (1.5-3 mm) with dark brown borders and grayish-white centers dotted with tiny black pycnidia.
Tomato___Septoria_leaf_spot.possible_causes: Fungus Septoria lycopersici spread by rain splashes and mechanical handling.
prevention: Destroy all crop debris after final harvest.
Apply organic or plastic mulch around plant bases.
Practice strict 2-year crop rotation.
management: Apply Mancozeb 75 WP (2.5 g/L) or Zineb 75 WP (2 g/L) at first sign of lower leaf spotting.
Prune off infected lower leaves and dispose away from the field.

Tomato___Spider_mites.symptoms: Fine yellow stippling or bronzing on upper leaf surfaces, with fine silken webbing visible on undersides; leaves turn brittle and drop.
Tomato___Spider_mites.possible_causes: Tetranychus urticae mites proliferating rapidly in hot, dry, dusty field conditions.
prevention: Keep field borders and access paths free of dusty weeds.
Maintain adequate irrigation to avoid plant water stress.
Conserve predatory mites and ladybird beetles.
management: Spray wettable sulphur 80 WP @ 3 g/L or Propargite 57 EC @ 2 ml/L.
Apply neem seed kernel extract (NSKE 5%) or Neem Oil (5 ml/L).
Wash leaves with high-pressure water spray where feasible.

Tomato___Target_Spot.symptoms: Brown circular lesions with faint concentric rings appearing on both leaves and fruit; infected leaves turn yellow and drop.
Tomato___Target_Spot.possible_causes: Fungus Corynespora cassiicola thriving in warm, tropical conditions with prolonged leaf wetness.
prevention: Improve air circulation through trellising and suckering.
Avoid working in fields when plants are wet.
Rotate with non-solanaceous crops.
management: Apply Azoxystrobin 23 SC @ 1 ml/L or Chlorothalonil 75 WP @ 2 g/L.
Ensure thorough coverage of both upper and lower leaf surfaces.

Tomato___Yellow_Leaf_Curl_Virus.symptoms: Severe plant stunting, erect bushy growth, upward leaf curling ('cupping'), marginal yellowing, and drastic flower drop.
Tomato___Yellow_Leaf_Curl_Virus.possible_causes: Begomovirus transmitted exclusively by the sweetpotato whitefly (Bemisia tabaci).
prevention: Install yellow sticky traps (15-20 per acre) for early whitefly monitoring.
Use 40-50 mesh insect-proof netting in nurseries.
Plant TYLCV-tolerant hybrids (e.g. US 440, NS 501).
management: Control whitefly vectors using Acetamiprid 20 SP (0.3 g/L) or Spiromesifen 22.9 SC (1 ml/L).
Rogue and immediately bag and destroy infected symptomatic plants.
Spray systemic insecticides or neem oil (3 ml/L) at nursery stage.

Tomato___Mosaic_virus.symptoms: Mottled light and dark green mosaic patterns on foliage, distorted 'shoestring' or fern-like leaves, and uneven fruit ripening.
Tomato___Mosaic_virus.possible_causes: Tobamovirus mechanically transmitted via contaminated hands, clothing, pruning shears, and infected seed.
prevention: Disinfect hands and pruning shears in 20% non-fat dry milk solution.
Wash hands with soap and water after handling tobacco products.
Use certified virus-free seed.
management: No chemical cure exists for viral plant infections.
Promptly rogue and incinerate infected plants.
Control aphids and thrips to prevent secondary pathogen stress.

Tomato___Healthy.symptoms: Vigorous lush green canopy, dark green foliage, healthy flower clusters, and clean developing fruit.
Tomato___Healthy.possible_causes: Clean seed stock, good sanitation, staking, drip irrigation, and balanced nutrition.
prevention: Continue preventative bi-weekly sprays of neem-based formulations.
Maintain drip irrigation schedule and support stakes.
management: No chemical pesticide required.
Apply water-soluble 19-19-19 @ 5 g/L during flowering and fruiting.
